criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: Six of nine frames carry a real physical subject. The wafer boats on 1, 3, 4 and 5 are modelled, cast and graded, and slide 6's relief counts check out: 12, 4 and a cleaved half, and 19 with no end stop. Slide 7's copper relief reads as two mountain silhouettes with crumbs at feed size. Slide 2 is a flat terracotta tile labelled 'Lubbock County' on a textured grid, and machine_qa flags busy art under that label. Slide 9's plate has cast_fraction 0.136 and reads as a flat UI mock. Slide 1's cover is a murky brown mid-tone with translucent wafers that blur at 432 px. On 2, 6, 7 and 9 the art sits in a bottom band under a type block.

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: The wafer-per-$1M motif runs through 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8, and the contact sheet reads as one dark, warm-copper deck. Frames 2, 7 and 9 switch to a flat top-down relief, so the filmstrip splits into two registers. Slide 8 brings the boat back as 'servers', which muddies the motif.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: Every numeral traces, the drawing units are declared in figures.json, and all three sources are primary Texas Tech Now pages. 'Over' and 'roughly' are kept honestly, and slide 6 refuses a total. Two leans: the cover's 'a cluster not built yet' is an inference from 'will help establish' (c4), and c18 and c19 rest on a university page because gov.texas.gov was off limits.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: A Texan learns what happened, who decided it, where, and that no install date exists. Nothing tells the reader what they can do, and the close is a rhetorical question. The stake stays general.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The cover hook earns a swipe. Frame 2 is an administrative note with the weakest art. Slides 3 to 5 are a chronological award history, and slide 6 restates the same three numbers. The real turn comes only at 9, and slides 7 and 8 sit between history and close without building to it.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: Clean and on house rules. It reads as an auditor more than a Texan. 'Drawn to illustrate' six times over. No Lubbock or South Plains specificity beyond the place name. 'The cluster is servers working as one system' is stilted.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: No topic repeat. The subject sits close to no. 73, a university research-computing cluster. The structure is the same 'one drawn object per unit' move as nos. 73, 75 and 76, and the dark-field copper palette matches 73 and 76.

one_sentence_fix: Cut slide 6, the restated award tally, and rebuild slide 2 so frame 2 pays off the cover with the November boat beside an empty IN SERVICE slot.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The copper relief reads as two mountain silhouettes with scattered crumbs, not epitaxial growth, and is disconnected from the wafer motif.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Replace it with a single wafer under a raking side light, with a raised faceted epitaxial layer growing across half its face in copper.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: A flat terracotta tile on a textured grid; the label sits on busy texture.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Model a lit relief of the Texas outline in dark stone with Lubbock County raised in copper, and seat the label in the quiet field beside it.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The cover sits in a murky brown mid-tone; translucent wafers smear at 432 px.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Light the boat with one hard rim key from frame left onto opaque polished silicon against a black field, so each of the 19 edges catches a bright line.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: cast_fraction 0.136; reads as a flat UI form and the empty IN SERVICE slot is not lit as focal.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Drop the key to a low raking angle so the slots cast deep shadows, and put a single warm pool on the empty IN SERVICE recess.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The 'servers' are drawn as another wafer boat with a screen.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Model a short rack of black server sleds on the same bench, one pulled out showing a bare socket.
